newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates close down, primary drop seen.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates close down, primary drop seen.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate pared early declines to close 17 basis points down at 21.73 percent, as dealers who hung on to paper dumped it in late trade.
"The late surge was due to those who did not want to be left holding paper," a trader said, who placed the session average at 21.30 percent.
"There was plenty of liquidity, however, and as long as the peso is not under substantial pressure, there should be no (liquidity) problems in the money market," he added.
Traders added that there was more liquidity in the term market than in many recent sessions, due to expectations that primary Cetes rates would fall at Tuesday's evening's central bank auction.
A Reuters survey of 10 money market traders showed they expected the bellwether 28-day Cete to fall an average of 22 basis points to 22.84 percent.

Cetes at 91-day and 182-day rates closed at 25.00 and 26.90 percent, respectively, compared with last week's primary rates of 25.63 and 27.33 percent. Overnight bank rates, meanwhile, closed 40 basis points down at 23.45 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 4.433 billion pesos of liquidity into the market by auctioning four credits. The lowest assignment rate was 23.83 percent.
Total credit maturities for Wednesday were estimated at 8.207 billion pesos. Traders said ensuing liquidity shortages may be offset by government spending of about 1.8 billion pesos.
